name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Full lifecycle: greenfield genesis (architect → explore → design) → roadmap briefs → /spec:sketch → /spec:plan → optional /spec:design (mock-bound, deterministic fidelity gates) → /spec:build (direct Sonnet worker dispatch per layer wave, executed red-check) → /spec:review (deterministic legs via review-legs.js + ONE fresh-context reviewer whose non-soft findings carry executed repros; verdict derived by verdict.js) → /spec:release, plus /spec:atlas, /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:escape, /spec:replay. Changelog (last 3): 7.6.0 — replay scratch write access: `block-cross-worktree-writes.sh` now allows a cross-worktree Write/Edit whose TARGET tree's private git dir carries the `replay-worktree` marker — the mutation-authoring worker's sanctioned path into the replay scratch tree, closing the gap that had the first live run's worker blocked on Edit/Write and tunneling the same write through Bash — keyed on the target only, so a session anchored inside the scratch tree writing OUT to the main checkout still blocks, and every unmarked cross-worktree block, same-tree allow, and git/parse fail-open arm is unchanged; replay.md's Phase 1 setup gate now runs `git clean -fd` after its `git checkout -- .` restore, since checkout alone cannot remove files `setupCommand` *creates* (the same run left an untracked root `package-lock.json` that would have polluted the blind reviewer's tree) and clean cannot touch the marker living outside the working tree; and reviewer.md gains a return-contract section stating the verdict field's closed vocabulary (`CLEAN`/`REVIEWER_FAILED`) its consumers (`replay.js --score`, verdict.js) already enforce. 7.5.0 — replay first-run fixes: `--score` derives caught/ambiguous/missed from the mutation's own patch hunks instead of a single worker-reported file/line, so a multi-file mutation (the now-unbound `self-consistent-polarity` pair, which may span two File Plan files or co-locate in one) scores on any of its sites; a dismissed ambiguous adjudication now records `unresolved` instead of nothing; replay.md's Phase 1 gains a setup gate that runs the host's `setupCommand` inside the scratch worktree and records `setup-failed` on a non-zero exit, then restores tracked files before class selection; `--apply` gains a required `--patch-out` and becomes the harness's only patch emitter, under pinned git config that survives hostile `diff.noprefix`/`core.quotePath` host settings, and commits via `git apply --index` rather than `git add -A` so setup-gate churn never contaminates the diff the blind reviewer reads; `--due`/`--select`/`--stats` treat `unresolved`/`setup-failed` as non-measurement rows that never enter the catch-rate denominator or reset the due clock; `replay-corpus.md`'s `dead-wiring` recipe requires the severed value land in a consumed-but-ignored sink, never a stranded local a strict-lint gate would flag on its own. 7.4.0 — scheduled mutation replay: new /spec:replay + replay.js harness inject one hand-authored corpus-class defect (spec/doctrine/replay-corpus.md, 6 classes) into a just-CLEANed spec's tree in a marker-guarded scratch worktree and dispatch the standard reviewer blind to it; catch/miss/leg-caught lands as a `stage:"replay"` ledger row plus a retained evidence artifact, and `replay.js --stats` derives the catch-rate; /spec:review's CLEAN close now warns when a replay is due (every 5th review, at minimum once per major version); core.md § Feedback Loop names the cadence policy and rules a sustained miss-rate as the evidence that reopens the second-reviewer question.
